1
Lesson 1 · Login page

Sign in

Get into the panel with your email, your password and a one-time code.

12345
  1. 1Enter your email.
  2. 2Enter your password.
  3. 3Select Login. A code is emailed to you. Type it in the Email verification box and select Verify now. No code? Wait for the countdown, select Resend, and check your spam folder.
  4. 4Forgot your password? Select this link to get a reset link by email.
  5. 5Switch the whole panel to Arabic (right-to-left). You can switch back at any time from the top bar.

Lesson 2 · Overview → Dashboard

Read the dashboard

See where registration stands, and print it for a meeting.

12345
  1. 1Filters (category, seniority, status, region, industry, date) change every figure on the page.
  2. 2Switch between All registrations, Confirmed, Declined and No reply.
  3. 3Key figures: registered, confirmed, new today, badges printed, check-ins, pending requests.
  4. 4Print report prints the page as a landscape report, stamped with the time.
  5. 5By Time: click a day to see only that day. Click any bar or slice to filter the page, and click it again to clear.

3
Lesson 3 · Overview → Guests

Find guests and export a list

Narrow the guest list down to the people you need, then download it.

123456
  1. 1Fill in what you know: status, category, attending, Reg ID, name, email, phone or date.
  2. 2Add filter for more, such as company, nationality, reconfirmation or companions.
  3. 3Select Search.
  4. 4Reset clears every filter.
  5. 5Export: All (Excel), Export Guests or Equipment lists (ZIP).
  6. 6New Guest: choose the category, fill in its form and save.
Filter first

With filters on, Export downloads only the guests you filtered. With no filters, it downloads everyone you're allowed to see.

Admin Panel Tutorial · TOURISE 2027Page 3 of 22
4
Lesson 4 · Overview → Guests

Review a guest

Open a registration, check it, then accept, hold or reject it. The buttons sit at the end of each guest's row.

12345
6789
  1. 1See more (eye) opens the guest's details.
  2. 2Edit (pencil) opens their form. Its Logistics tab holds flights and hotel.
  3. 3Accept (✓), then Confirm. The guest gets the category's accept email.
  4. 4Hold (pause) sets the guest On-hold. No message is sent.
  5. 5Reject (✕) sends the category's reject message.
3
  1. 6Personal info: every answer on the guest's form.
  2. 7Email history: every email sent to this guest.
  3. 8Guest Actions History: who changed what, and when.
  4. 9Edit and Hold are also at the top of the details.

Pending guests show ✓ Hold ✕. Accepted guests show Resend, SMS, WhatsApp, Print, Collect and e-badge instead. To reopen a rejected guest, use Hold first.

Admin Panel Tutorial · TOURISE 2027Page 4 of 22
5
Lesson 5 · Overview → Invitations → New Invitation

Send invitations

Invite a list of people to a private category (VIP, Speaker, Sponsor and others).

12345678
  1. 1Single: one link per guest. Multiple: one shared link for several people.
  2. 2Give the batch a name.
  3. 3Choose the category they're invited to.
  4. 4Pick the channel: email, SMS or WhatsApp.
  5. 5Prefill data puts each guest's details into their form.
  6. 6Lock data stops them from changing those details.
  7. 7Enter the Quantity. Then choose to type the guests in (Manual) or upload an Excel list.
  8. 8Select Create. Open the new collection and select Send invitation, or Send in bulk.
Before you send

The email template must include {{ invitation_link }}, or guests get no link. Turning With form off makes it a save-the-date email with no registration link.

6
Lesson 6 · Overview → Invitation Requests

Handle invitation requests

People without an invitation can ask for one on the website or through a partner site. You decide each request here.

123456
  1. 1Search or filter by status, request category, source, date or industry.
  2. 2Request Categories: each request form's fields, target category, emails and OTP.
  3. 3Tick several pending requests to accept them together.
  4. 4See more shows the full request.
  5. 5Accept invites the person to the target category. Landed in shows the invitation they received.
  6. 6Reject sends the rejection email if one is set. Otherwise the person hears nothing.
Partner API keys

Partner websites send requests with their own key, under Operations → API keys. A key is shown only once, so copy it straight away.

Lesson 7 · Overview → Dignitary Parties

Follow a dignitary's party

A dignitary lists their delegation, security and protocol on their own form, and the system invites each person. You only watch and follow up.

Step 1The dignitary registers and lists their people (up to 30)
→
Step 2Each person gets a personal invitation email
→
Step 3Their form opens pre-filled and linked to the dignitary
→
Step 4They appear here under the dignitary
123
  1. 1Invitation email: choose the template for all three groups. Do this first. Until you do, invitations are created but not emailed.
  2. 2Search by name, registration number or email.
  3. 3Each dignitary's Delegation, Security and Protocol: who has registered, who hasn't, and whether their email was sent. Use Send / Resend, or Invite someone they left out.

In the Guests list, a party member's row shows Invited by and the dignitary's name.

8
Lesson 8 · Management → Categories → Edit

Set up a category

Every guest belongs to a category. The category decides their form, who may register, the status they get and the messages they receive.

12345
  1. 1Tabs. Only General settings and Form configuration are required. Communications sets which email, SMS or WhatsApp goes out on register, accept and reject.
  2. 2Visibility. Private needs an invitation. Public is an open link.
  3. 3Status. Active turns the category on.
  4. 4Status configuration. Sets the status a guest gets when they register, and when you accept or reject them.
  5. 5Select Save.
Tip

To start faster, use Clone on a similar category in the Categories list. Use the Admin access tab to add the new category to scoped admins in one step.

Lesson 9 · Communications → Automation → Create

Message many guests at once

Send one template to a whole group, such as every accepted speaker, or change their status together.

12345
  1. 1Choose who with the filters: status, category, attending and more.
  2. 2Select Search.
  3. 3Select all matching takes everyone in the result.
  4. 4Or tick guests one by one.
  5. 5Run automation: pick the template and channel (or the status change), then when to run it.
Large sends

Choose Run manually after review. The automation is saved without sending, so you can check the list and start it with Run now.

Lesson 10 · Communications → Emails and Logs

Templates and sent messages

Write the emails guests receive, then check that they went out.

12
  1. 1New Email template, with an English and an Arabic version.
  2. 2Open the editor to write it. Variables like {{ full_name }} and {{ qr_code }} fill in per guest.
345
  1. 3Logs → Guest Emails: search by email, workflow, token or registration number.
  2. 4Workflow: which step sent the email, for example on accept.
  3. 5Sent, Delivered, Open, Error: check here first when a guest says they got nothing.
  4. •A new template only goes out once it's picked in a category's Communications tab (Lesson 8).

Lesson 11 · Operations → Gate scanning

Scan guests at the gate

Check guests in at an entrance with an iPad camera or a handheld scanner.

123
  1. 1Select your gate.
  2. 2Enter the iPad number.
  3. 3Select Save. Then choose Camera or Device scanner and scan each badge.
  4. •“Guest not found”? Search by name, or capture the badge photo.
12
Lesson 12 · Management → Admins → Create

Add an admin

Give a colleague access to exactly what they need, and nothing more.

123456
  1. 1Role decides what they can do. Use Manage roles to create one.
  2. 2Enter their name, email and phone.
  3. 3Data scope: the categories and statuses they may see.
  4. 4Send setup email (recommended) lets them set their own password.
  5. 5Keep Require OTP on login on.
  6. 6Select Create. Then ask them to sign in and check their guest list.
Empty scope = no guests

An admin with no categories and no statuses sees no guests, whatever the hint on the form says. Super Admins see everyone.

Lesson 13 · Management → Roles → Create

Create a role

A role decides what an admin can do. Everyone who holds the role gets exactly the same permissions.

1234
  1. 1Name the role in English and Arabic.
  2. 2Select all or Deselect all for every screen at once.
  3. 3Or tick a whole section at once, such as Dashboard.
  4. 4Tick single actions: View, Export, Accept, Print and so on. Then save.
14
Lesson 14 · Management → Guest Status, Titles · Operations → Countries

Statuses, titles and countries

The lists your forms and reports use. Set them once, before registration opens.

1234
  1. 1New Guest Status adds a status.
  2. 2Order sets where it appears in lists.
  3. 3Color is the badge colour shown across the panel.
  4. 4Edit, view, switch on or off, or delete. Never delete a status that's in use.

Titles (Mr., Dr., H.E. and more) set the gender each applies to, and whether it shows on the badge and the form. Countries hold English and Arabic names, the country code and the phone code.

Lesson 15 · Communications → Emails

Email settings and mail servers

Set these up once, so every email the system sends has the right event name and goes out through a working mail server.

12345
  1. 1Basic Configuration: the event name used in emails.
  2. 2System templates: emails the system sends by itself, such as the login code.
  3. 3Add to calendar: the event details behind calendar links.
  4. 4Enter the event name in English and Arabic.
  5. 5Select Save.
678
  1. 6New SMTP configuration adds a mail server (host, port, sender address).
  2. 7Default: the server every email uses unless a category picks another.
  3. 8The paper-plane icon sends a test email. Use it after every change.
  4. •A new admin’s setup email needs a default mail server.

Lesson 16 · Communications → SMS and WhatsApp

SMS and WhatsApp

These work like email: a provider to send through, templates to send, and a log to check.

123
  1. 1New WhatsApp template, with an English and an Arabic version.
  2. 2Purpose: what the template is for.
  3. 3The paper-plane icon sends a test WhatsApp.
ChannelSet up underCheck what was sent
SMSSMS → Templates · SMS provider configsLogs → Guest SMS · Invitation SMS
WhatsAppWhatsApp → templates · config · provider configsWhatsApp → Guest WhatsApp · Invitation WhatsApp
Provider first

Until a provider config is added, the Send SMS and Send WhatsApp buttons stay grey and say “provider not configured”. WhatsApp config holds the event details that WhatsApp messages fill in.

Lesson 17 · Operations → Guest Drafts

Follow up unfinished registrations

People who started a registration form but never submitted it. The list is read-only.

1234
  1. 1Search by first name, last name, email or phone.
  2. 2Phone OTP Sent / Verified: how far they got with the phone check.
  3. 3The eye icon shows everything they filled in.
  4. 4Export the list to follow people up.
Personal data

Drafts hold the details of people who never finished registering. Only give this screen to the people who follow them up.

Lesson 19 · Operations → API keys

Give a partner website a key

Partner websites can send invitation requests and newsletter sign-ups straight into the panel. Each site gets its own key.

12345
  1. 1Type the website name.
  2. 2Select Issue a key, then copy the key at once. It's shown only this one time.
  3. 3After that, only the start of the key is shown, with requests filed and when it was last used.
  4. 4Revoke switches one site off without touching the others.
  5. 5Copy guide as text and send it to the partner's developer.

Lesson 20 · Operations → Newsletter

Send a newsletter

Subscribers come from the opt-in on registration forms and from the website. Send them a designed newsletter.

12345
  1. 1Tabs: Subscribers, Dashboard, Lists, Campaigns and Newsletter Templates.
  2. 2Filter by email, status, source or list.
  3. 3Tick the subscribers you want.
  4. 4Add to list groups them, for example for one audience.
  5. 5Send Newsletter: pick a template, and send to your selection or to a whole list.
  6. •Unsubscribed people are skipped automatically, even if ticked.

Build the design first under Newsletter Templates (English and Arabic). Campaigns shows every send with sent, opened and clicked counts. Subscribers and templates can't be deleted. Use Block to retire a template.

Lesson 21 · Operations → Badges → New Badge

Design a badge

Set the badge size and layout, and which categories use it.

123456
  1. 1Name the design in English and Arabic.
  2. 2Pick a common size, such as Standard, Slim or ID-card…
  3. 3… or type your own height and width in millimetres.

Lesson 22 · Operations → Gates scans

Areas, gates and the scan log

Set up the venue before the event: areas first, then the gates in each area.

1234
  1. 1Name the gate in English and Arabic.
  2. 2Choose the Area it belongs to.
  3. 3Status: Active gates can scan.
  4. 4Select Create.
ScreenWhat it's for
AreasZones of the venue, such as the main hall or the VIP lounge. The admins who work there are assigned on the area.
GatesEntrances. Each belongs to an area, and the list shows which iPad it's assigned to.
ScansEvery scan, with total and unique visitors. You can export it.

Gate staff then scan on Gate scanning (Lesson 11).

Lesson 23 · Logistics → Hotels · Guests → Logistics

Hotels and a guest's travel

For hosted guests: set up the hotels, then record each guest's flights and room.

1234
  1. 1Enter the hotel name.
  2. 2Reserved at: the booking date.
  3. 3Keep the Status Active.
  4. 4Select Create. Then open the hotel and add its rooms, with how many are booked and how many remain.
5678910

Open a guest in Guests, select Edit, then open the Logistics page:

  1. 5Flights info tab.
  2. 6Accommodation info tab: hotel, room, check-in and check-out.
  3. 7Traveling Status: where the guest's travel stands. The list lives under Logistics → Traveling Status.
  4. 8Self booking: the guest books their own travel.
  5. 9Arrival: date, time, city, flight and terminal.
  6. 10Departure: the same for the way home. Pickup is suggested 3 hours before departure. Save at the bottom.

Handle e-visas

Every guest who needs a visa, and where each one stands, from package to issued visa.

123456

Quick help

When something doesn't work

ProblemWhat to doLesson
My guest list is emptyAsk a Super Admin to add categories and statuses to your data scope12
A menu item is missingYour role doesn't include it. Ask for it to be added.12
No login code arrivedWait for the countdown, select Resend, and check spam1
A guest got no emailCheck Logs → Guest Emails, then the category's Communications tab10, 8
A button says “provider not configured”That channel (SMS or WhatsApp) isn't set up yet. Ask the technical team.—
A dignitary's party got no invitationsChoose the Invitation email on Dignitary Parties, then Send7
An invitation link is “not valid”The link was already used, or its collection is inactive. Send a new one.5
There's no Accept buttonThe guest isn't Pending or On-hold. Use Hold first to reopen them.4
There's no Export buttonYour role doesn't include Export12
A scanned badge shows “Guest not found”Search by name, or capture the badge photo11
No emails go out at allCheck there is a default mail server, and send a test email15
A partner site can't send requestsCheck its key isn't revoked, or issue a new one19
A newsletter skipped some peopleThey unsubscribed. Unsubscribed people are always skipped.20
More detail

What each role can do is in the Administrator Access & Roles guide. Everything else is in the online TOURISE Admin Guide.
